results.title: Applying Program Theory Innovation Model for ECLSS Development for India?s Gaganyaan Human Space Flight Program
results.abstract: The Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO) implements the national space activities under the policy direction of the Space Commission constituted within the Department of Space (DoS), Government of India that directly reports to the Prime Minister of India. The stated vision of ISRO is to ?Harness, sustain and augment space technology for national development, while pursuing space science research and planetary exploration.? Over the past five decades, ISRO has established India as a leading spacefaring nation through the Indian Remote Sensing (IRS) satellites program for civilian earth observation and disaster management, the Indian National Satellites (INSAT) program for telecommunications and broadband network, Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), and through dedicated planetary and astronomy space science missions. In 2018, the Indian government committed the nation to pursuing human spaceflight with a budget allocation of ?10,000 Crores (~ $1.4 billion) and subsequently provide a net additional funding of ?11,170 Crore in 2024, with the objective to spur R&D in the nation and enable India to participate in future global space exploration endeavors for national benefits. In January 2019, ISRO established the Human Space Flight Center (HSFC) and is currently embarking on an ambitious ?Gaganyaan? program to realize human spaceflight capabilities within the nation, to undertake a crewed mission by 2027-28 to carry a crew of up to three to Low Earth Orbit (LEO) for up to three days and return them safely to Indian sea waters and from 2028 to begin missions to establish the Indian Space Station, ?Bharatiya Antariksh Station? (BAS), in a circular Low Earth Orbit (LEO) of about 400-450 km by 2035. The Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS) that provides a safe and habitable environment for Crew Health & Performance (CHP) in the harsh conditions of space is the most critical component for any human spaceflight (HSF) mission. The development of ECLSS is a strategic capability in the space domain that only a few countries have achieved. In this paper, I provide the stakeholder & technical requirements and the structure of the major ECLSS subsystems through MBSE SysML diagrams. Given the significance and novel nature of ECLSS development for India?s emerging human spaceflight program, I then applied the innovation model from program theory to develop and understand the outcomes chain for the ECLSS Innovation.

results.title: On-Orbit Digital Twin for Spacecraft Battery State and Health Estimation
results.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are mission-critical for nearly every modern spacecraft, yet their on-orbit management remains dominated by conservative, heuristic flight rules that sacrifice usable energy and operational flexibility to avoid degradation. This paper presents a lightweight battery digital-twin framework built around a dual extended Kalman filter (Dual-EKF) coupled with an equivalent-circuit model. A fast filter tracks state of charge (SOC) at every measurement sample, while a slow filter estimates capacity for real-time state-of-health (SOH) monitoring. On-board battery capacity forecasts are correlated with periodic reference performance tests (RPTs) and compared to the digital twin prediction. The framework is validated in the laboratory on EEMB LIR-2032 coin cells and currently on orbit aboard the Proteus Space Mercury One spacecraft, which carries a dedicated cycling payload with three Li-ion coin cells. Ground testing achieves a voltage-prediction RMSE below 5 mV and capacity estimation within 2% of RPT-derived values; preliminary on-orbit results show consistent SOC convergence, capacity-fade trends in line with ground priors, and graceful behavior under telemetry dropouts. We also outline a short future-work direction: a Gaussian-process-based lithium plating detector that would add degradation-mechanism awareness to the digital twin, enabling operators to distinguish aging from damaging plating events.

results.title: Test and Evaluation Procedure to Develop a Digital Twin of the Sleeper-Sat
results.abstract: A Digital Twin (DT) is not just a collection of static digital models at the component level of a physical system but a dynamic entity that evolves in parallel with the physical system it mirrors. This evolution starts with physics-based or data-driven physics models representing the physical system and advances to Authoritative Virtualization or DT through continuous data assimilation and ongoing Digital Engineering Test and Evaluation processes. This paper aims to create a mathematical framework for the DE Test and Evaluation Process, which incorporates data assimilation to link physical and digital models, uncertainty quantification, uncertainty propagation, and DT calibration process. This framework will enable the DT to perform operations, control, decision-making, and predictions at scale. The framework will be implemented to develop the DT of the Sleeper-sat to analyze the Sleeper-sat's structural deformation during its deployment in space. The Sleeper-sat will be a variant of previously constructed Sleeper-sats from the Aerospace Center at UTEP. The DT of the Sleeper-sat will be capable of predicting and monitoring structural health during its space operations.

results.title: Digitally-assisted Development of a Space Robotic Arm for Small Satellites Applications
results.abstract: In-space servicing, assembly, and manufacturing (ISAM) expands space-based capabilities by extending satellite lifespans and decoupling spacecraft design from launch vehicle constraints. Robotic systems are proposed to support multiple aspects of ISAM missions, from capture and manipulation to manufacturing and repair. Consequently, the rapid development and testing of diverse robotic platforms is imperative to meet the evolving demands of the new space enterprise. This paper proposes a digital engineering framework to expedite the design, development, testing, and operation analysis of space robotic platforms. Digital engineering design tools are employed to optimize design for space environment operations; additionally, traditional manufacturing methods are streamlined with integrated wireless communication; IoT (Internet of thing) capabilities enable cloud-based modification to adjust to dynamic design requirements. Leveraging Amazon Web Services cloud-based servers, a digital twin of the robotic arm will be developed to assist the project's life cycle, from design to evaluation and test. AWS IoT communication protocols enable near real-time transmission of robotic arm sensor data to its digital twin. Siemens NX CAE (Computer Aided Engineering) facilitates photorealistic physics-based simulation, optimizing robotic arm control and motion planning. The paper details the digital engineering implementation of a two-degree-of-freedom robotic arm featuring piezoelectric rotary motors, applied in a zero gravity simulation air-bearing table study.

results.title: Leveraging a Digital Engineering Testbed to Explore Mission Resilience for New Observing Strategies
results.abstract: View Video Presentation: https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2023-0257.vidThis study introduces the New Observing Strategies Testbed (NOS-T); a digital engineering environment to conduct coordinated experiments between independent and potentially geographically distributed nodes. The testbed supports both real-time applications and scaled-time simulations. NOS-T is built on an event-driven architecture where applications communicate via message payloads mediated by an event-broker. This allows for collaboration across organizational boundaries while maintaining autonomy and control over the flow of information. Testbed capabilities are demonstrated for an example problem exploring data downlink opportunities for two distinct ground network systems. A twenty-four hour mission is simulated for two Earth observing satellites in sun-synchronous orbits, with various iterations of traditional single arctic ground stations with fixed cost contracts versus newer commercial ground stations with on-demand cost models. Results demonstrate the capability of the commercial ground stations to maintain significant data margins throughout the mission with considerable cost-savings from the on-demand pricing.

results.title: EssentialSAT: A Space Systems Engineering Learning Laboratory
results.abstract: View Video Presentation: https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2022-4207.vidAs the space industry expands to include start-up companies and emerging space nations, there is pressing need for technical workforce development. Paper-based ?book learning? only takes us so far. Real hardware and software behave differently than models predict. The EssentialSAT desktop space system was developed to address this challenge. This low-cost, desktop satellite simulator system provides a unique, hands-on learning experience as a part of an integrated space systems engineering curriculum. EssentialSAT provides an educational kit of representative spacecraft subsystems that can be assembled, integrated, and tested in the classroom with simple ground support equipment. The discussion of EssentialSAT development highlights the application of an integrated digital ecosystem that includes CAD, eCAD, addictive manufacturing and all orchestrated using model-based systems engineering (MBSE). Its use as part of a classroom experience that allows students to learn about individual spacecraft subsystems?power, data handling, communication, attitude determination and control, remote sensing, mechanisms?as well as the assembly, integration and verification and operation of the entire system. The paper describes details of the system elements and interfaces. Conclusions describe describe future applications and its potential available as an open-source design.

results.title: Digital Engineering Development in an Academic CubeSat Project
results.abstract: Digital engineering is increasingly introduced for managing and supporting the development of systems for space. However, few academic teams have the competency needed to manage projects using digital engineering and systems engineering. The subject of this paper is an academic CubeSat project in which a variety of digital engineering techniques are used. The tailoring that has been applied to fit the academic environment including students from different disciplines and levels of maturity is described. This paper shows how a customized Scrum methodology for hardware and software integrated with a workflow in a digital tool environment has given positive results for both the team and the system development. This paper also discusses how to introduce new members to the team and how to train them to work with digital engineering as a multidisciplinary team. This paper presents how the systems engineering and project management activities have been integrated into the academic CubeSat project, evaluate how well this fusion worked, and estimate its potential to be used as a guide for other digital engineering projects.

results.title: Programmatic Management for the ABEX CubeSat in a Model Based System Engineering Environment
results.abstract: View Video Presentation: https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2021-0623.vidThis paper describes how the systems engineering team has applied a Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) methodology to the Alabama Burst Energetics eXplorer (ABEX) project, formerly known as the Alabama Experiment for In-situ Shielding (AEGIS). The MBSE approach is based around the development of an Integrated Systems Model (ISM) that contains a model of the system and most of the programmatic information about the project. This paper details how the programmatic aspects of the projects were adapted to be recorded and tracked in the ISM.

results.title: Using a Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) Variant Approach for Architecting Signal Processing in a Space-Based Sensor
results.abstract: Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) can be used to develop the architecture of a space-based sensor. The process begins with the development of use cases (UCs) of a general system model for a sensor processor which is composed of both hardware and software-based elements. Domain-specific UC?s can then be created and linked to the general level. This process continues through the modeling of variances in system behavior, including activity, sequence and state diagrams. This is done in parallel with the development of structural model instances that represent the configuration of the system for the specific domain being considered. The result is an end-to-end extensible sensor model that can then be applied to analyze the end-to-end signal processing chain.
